authority.rule: Recovered family names, Path implementation names and physical actions outrank this registry. Development causality is DERIVED unless independently sourced. Numeric constants remain PROPOSED unless separately adopted.

families.operator: Manipulate effective local metric so a protected volume traverses a reduced proper route length.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Solve a static, weak metric perturbation over a fixed laboratory volume.
stages.physicalAdvance: Massive fixed emitters, crude field cages and sacrificial sinks tolerate poor symmetry.
stages.distanceEffect: No practical transit; establishes measurable reduction of proper interval.
stages.safetyEffect: Manual exclusion volume; abort is power removal.
stages.maintenanceEffect: Frequent emitter replacement and alignment survey.
stages.signatureEffect: Extreme thermal/EM output for tiny metric effect.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Solve directed front-back compression rather than isotropic perturbation.
stages.physicalAdvance: Phased emitter sectors and better timing references reduce wasted modes.
stages.distanceEffect: Useful local inertial relief and sublight metric assistance.
stages.maintenanceEffect: Phase calibration becomes primary service burden.
stages.signatureEffect: Narrower but still conspicuous spool field.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Close a moving three-dimensional boundary around payload volume.
stages.physicalAdvance: Distributed emitters, active mounts and structural strain feedback maintain enclosure.
stages.distanceEffect: Sustained compressed-route travel becomes operational below causal horizon limits.
stages.safetyEffect: Coverage margin and hull-strain aborts become mandatory.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Include horizon formation and exit solvability as explicit constraints.
stages.physicalAdvance: Forward gravimetry, higher-speed controllers and recovery sinks support safe superluminal envelopes.
stages.distanceEffect: First practical FTL metric routes.
stages.safetyEffect: Sensor horizon must exceed solve-command-field-exit horizon.
stages.maintenanceEffect: Navigation and recovery systems become co-equal with emitters.
stages.signatureEffect: Sharper emergence ringing but reduced waste heat per distance.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Continuously solve multi-sector tensor field under changing gravity.
stages.physicalAdvance: Redundant local controllers, better active materials and isolated sectors permit fleet operation.
stages.distanceEffect: Longer uninterrupted interstellar legs and tighter gravity tolerance.
stages.safetyEffect: Regional degradation can be shed without whole-envelope collapse.
stages.signatureEffect: Lower parasitic modes; family gravitational signature remains.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Optimize route and envelope jointly through gravitational terrain.
stages.physicalAdvance: Higher energy density, predictive gravimetry and stronger field materials increase stable gradient authority.
stages.distanceEffect: Strategic-range legs by reducing gravity-induced efficiency loss rather than raw multiplier alone.
stages.safetyEffect: Probabilistic route envelopes and precomputed fallback exits.
stages.maintenanceEffect: Reference calibration and material fatigue dominate.
stages.signatureEffect: High peak field with improved energy efficiency.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Real-time receding-horizon metric optimization with self-calibrating boundary model.
stages.physicalAdvance: Compact high-authority materials, dense sensing and distributed recovery shrink machinery volume.
stages.distanceEffect: Apex compact systems approach capital-drive route quality at much smaller scale.
stages.safetyEffect: Continuous re-solve expands usable abort margin without implying perfect safety.
stages.maintenanceEffect: Software/reference integrity and microsector health supersede gross alignment.
stages.signatureEffect: Shorter spool and cleaner closure; metric distortion remains detectable.

families.operator: Select and follow favorable geodesic/equipotential structure in naturally curved spacetime.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Map one fixed local gradient and demonstrate preferential coupling.
stages.physicalAdvance: Monumental gravitic resonators and fixed interferometers.
stages.distanceEffect: No general transit; proves gravity can be treated as navigable structure.
stages.safetyEffect: Operates only on surveyed static geometry.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Track a continuous local equipotential sheet.
stages.physicalAdvance: Distributed gradient sensors and controllable coupling surfaces.
stages.distanceEffect: Sublight high-efficiency travel along favorable wells.
stages.signatureEffect: Lower energy but persistent gravitic modulation.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Solve multi-body barycentric sheets and moving saddles.
stages.physicalAdvance: Ephemeris processors and faster field steering.
stages.distanceEffect: System-scale rapid transit via planetary/stellar geometry.
stages.safetyEffect: Predictive saddle crossing and branch rejection.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Extend solutions onto weak interstellar shear/lensing planes.
stages.physicalAdvance: Ultra-sensitive long-baseline gravimetry and high-coherence couplers.
stages.distanceEffect: First FTL hyperlane-like transit along natural shear structures.
stages.maintenanceEffect: Weak-signal sensors require obsessive reference maintenance.
stages.signatureEffect: Low onboard energy compared with route speed; strong coupling perturbation at transitions.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Treat candidate planes as a graph with branch probability and cost.
stages.physicalAdvance: Redundant forward sensing and rapid recoupling zones.
stages.distanceEffect: Can switch between planes instead of waiting for one ideal corridor.
stages.safetyEffect: Probabilistic fork handling and regional decouple.
stages.maintenanceEffect: Coupler-zone health and sensor consensus testing.
stages.signatureEffect: More frequent but smaller transition events.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Infer useful structure through incomplete mass maps and stronger curvature.
stages.physicalAdvance: Better dynamic range, structural isolation and model assimilation.
stages.distanceEffect: Greater route availability and closer approach to difficult gravity volumes.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Continuous receding-horizon geodesic rewriting as new mass information arrives.
stages.physicalAdvance: Dense distributed sensors/controllers and fast fail-safe decouplers.
stages.distanceEffect: Apex use of transient or previously unusable gravitational roads.
stages.safetyEffect: Maximum practical lookahead and branch-rejection margin.
stages.maintenanceEffect: Distributed reference trust and local actuator health dominate.

families.operator: Couple to a metastable Q-boundary shear while maintaining adhesion and phase-velocity match.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Identify repeatable Q-boundary states and measure shear flow.
stages.physicalAdvance: Fixed resonators and sacrificial probes.
stages.distanceEffect: Observation only.
stages.signatureEffect: Large Q excitation from inefficient coupling.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Solve short-lived phase match for instrument packages.
stages.physicalAdvance: Fast phase vanes and expendable adhesion coils.
stages.distanceEffect: Short unmanned translations.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Stabilize a bounded artificial shear segment.
stages.physicalAdvance: Fixed tunnel emitters and boundary skins.
stages.distanceEffect: Reliable local macroscopic transfer.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Predict moving boundary flow and solve exit correspondence.
stages.physicalAdvance: Shipwide phase skin, Q-weather sensors and recovery dampers.
stages.distanceEffect: First autonomous interstellar slipstream transit.
stages.safetyEffect: Forward Q-weather horizon supports emergency de-transit.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Continuously regulate adhesion margin across multiple hull zones.
stages.physicalAdvance: Distributed local controllers and redundant phase references.
stages.distanceEffect: Longer stable rides through variable Q conditions.
stages.safetyEffect: Local adhesion failure need not cascade immediately.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Route through forecast Q-weather instead of reacting locally.
stages.physicalAdvance: Long-look sensors, higher-energy adhesion authority and predictive solvers.
stages.distanceEffect: Strategic route selection exploits faster stable shear bands.
stages.maintenanceEffect: Sensor calibration and energy-buffer health dominate.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Self-calibrating boundary estimator jointly solves adhesion, phase and exit state.
stages.physicalAdvance: Dense smart phase materials and compact recovery hardware.
stages.distanceEffect: High performance in smaller hulls with less dedicated machinery volume.
stages.maintenanceEffect: Material state and estimator integrity replace manual phasing.
stages.signatureEffect: Reduced spool signature; Q wake remains intrinsic.

families.operator: Translate protected state through indexed quantized Q addresses and valid phase epochs.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Prove stable discrete Q addresses exist.
stages.physicalAdvance: Monumental address resonator and precision references.
stages.distanceEffect: No payload translation.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Map adjacent address transitions for simple matter states.
stages.physicalAdvance: Small phase cages and epoch clocks.
stages.distanceEffect: Microscopic-to-small payload translation.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Maintain protected-state coverage over complex macroscopic payloads.
stages.physicalAdvance: Larger synchronized cage arrays and stronger state buffers.
stages.distanceEffect: Macroscopic local jumps.
stages.safetyEffect: Coverage and identity checks before execution.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Resolve remote address plus epoch against authenticated beacon references.
stages.physicalAdvance: Beacon network, long-baseline clocks and anti-alias discriminators.
stages.distanceEffect: First reliable interstellar discrete translations.
stages.signatureEffect: Correlated beacon and vessel phase events.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Search multi-hop address graphs without fixed paired infrastructure.
stages.physicalAdvance: Onboard route memory, stronger cages and fast epoch solvers.
stages.distanceEffect: Flexible multi-system routing.
stages.safetyEffect: Bad-address branches can be rejected before commit.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Optimize graph route for uncertainty, infrastructure trust and total transition cost.
stages.physicalAdvance: Dense beacon meshes and strategic reference services.
stages.distanceEffect: Strategic effective range through trusted multi-hop networks.
stages.safetyEffect: Redundant address authorities and route proofs.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Continuous anti-alias state estimation and compact graph solving.
stages.physicalAdvance: High-density phase materials, local reference synthesis and compact cages.
stages.distanceEffect: Small vessels achieve autonomous long-range lattice access.
stages.safetyEffect: Real-time alias rejection expands valid operating envelope.
stages.maintenanceEffect: Reference integrity and cage-state health dominate.

families.operator: Traverse a shorter admissible higher-dimensional geodesic and return through a stable projection map.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Detect and characterize accessible extra-dimensional degrees of freedom.
stages.physicalAdvance: Fixed topology sensors and high-energy excitation apparatus.
stages.distanceEffect: Observation only.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Solve one controlled embedding into an additional axis and back.
stages.physicalAdvance: Captive projection cage and return-map references.
stages.distanceEffect: Tiny controlled shortcut paths.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Compute bounded higher-dimensional geodesics for macroscopic payloads.
stages.physicalAdvance: Large synchronized manifold coils and structural isolation.
stages.distanceEffect: Reliable facility-scale shortcut transit.
stages.maintenanceEffect: Coil geometry and return references dominate.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Solve moving origin embedding and remote return map.
stages.physicalAdvance: Onboard manifold cage, navigation solver and return-field recovery.
stages.distanceEffect: First autonomous interstellar manifold routes.
stages.safetyEffect: Return-map condition number becomes hard go/no-go criterion.
stages.maintenanceEffect: Projection references equal prime mover in importance.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Search several dimensional axes and reject ill-conditioned return solutions.
stages.physicalAdvance: Multi-axis field hardware and higher-bandwidth solvers.
stages.distanceEffect: Shorter routes and more available endpoints.
stages.signatureEffect: More complex but lower-waste insertion spectrum.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Optimize geodesic, gravity interaction and return conditioning jointly over long baselines.
stages.physicalAdvance: Stronger field structures, better energy density and deep-space references.
stages.distanceEffect: Strategic deep-range shortcuts.
stages.maintenanceEffect: Field materials and reference drift dominate long missions.
stages.signatureEffect: High peak dimensional event with reduced duration.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Real-time multi-axis route/return optimization in a compact solver.
stages.physicalAdvance: Dense programmable field media and distributed return safeguards.
stages.distanceEffect: Capital-grade manifold choice in compact installations.
stages.maintenanceEffect: Reference/model integrity replaces gross alignment burden.
stages.signatureEffect: Short compact insertion pulse; topology disturbance remains.

families.operator: Temporarily alter topology so certified origin and destination volumes become adjacent.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Demonstrate microscopic temporary adjacency between nearby bounded regions.
stages.physicalAdvance: Fixed aperture rings and enormous topology-support structure.
stages.distanceEffect: Microscopic adjacency only.
stages.signatureEffect: Large topology ringing for tiny displacement.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Maintain adjacency across a finite protected cargo volume.
stages.physicalAdvance: Closed fold-volume panels, better boundary references and sinks.
stages.distanceEffect: Local macroscopic transfer.
stages.safetyEffect: Hard endpoint exclusion and chamber interlocks.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Solve paired separated endpoint volumes with stable correspondence.
stages.physicalAdvance: Two large fixed endpoint stations and authenticated ranging.
stages.distanceEffect: Long-range fixed-point folding.
stages.safetyEffect: Both endpoints independently certify occupancy and geometry.
stages.maintenanceEffect: Paired reference alignment becomes infrastructure task.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Treat the origin volume as moving shipboard geometry while solving remote adjacency.
stages.physicalAdvance: Shipboard topology waveguides, metric aperture rings, gravimetry and recovery dampers.
stages.distanceEffect: First autonomous interstellar fold-jumps.
stages.safetyEffect: Hard commit boundary; no meaningful steering after topology execution begins.
stages.maintenanceEffect: Waveguide geometry, references and ringing dampers are flight-critical.
stages.signatureEffect: Distinct spool, adjacency event and post-jump ringing.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Generate and rank multiple valid adjacency solutions under uncertainty.
stages.physicalAdvance: Redundant solvers, better endpoint sensors and sectional field hardware.
stages.distanceEffect: More destinations become safely reachable without prepared gates.
stages.safetyEffect: Alternative endpoint solutions permit conservative rejection.
stages.signatureEffect: Cleaner fold closure with less residual ringing.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Condition topology solution on long-baseline gravity/reference covariance and minimize manipulated separation subject to stability.
stages.physicalAdvance: Higher-authority field materials, stronger support structure and deep-range reference networks.
stages.distanceEffect: Strategic long-fold range comes from maintaining valid adjacency solutions across worse-conditioned endpoints.
stages.safetyEffect: Larger exclusion models and stronger precommit proof requirements.
stages.maintenanceEffect: Material fatigue and reference provenance dominate.
stages.signatureEffect: Higher peak topology stress but lower ringing per unit displacement.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Continuously update compact adjacency solutions until the last safe commit instant.
stages.physicalAdvance: Dense field media, local gravimetry and fast recovery architecture shrink the system.
stages.distanceEffect: High-quality folds from much smaller platforms; not unlimited range.
stages.safetyEffect: Maximum practical precommit correction window and rapid failed-spool recovery.
stages.maintenanceEffect: Microgeometry and reference-state health replace monumental alignment.
stages.signatureEffect: Very short high-intensity fold event with characteristic ringing tail.

families.operator: Maintain a multiply connected spacetime throat between synchronized mouths and move traffic through the aperture.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Create and measure a transient microscopic throat solution.
stages.physicalAdvance: Massive fixed exotic-field apparatus.
stages.distanceEffect: No usable transit.
stages.signatureEffect: Huge energy pulse and topology disturbance.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Stabilize a throat with finite radius and bounded mass flux.
stages.physicalAdvance: Aperture rings, throat supports and dedicated recovery plant.
stages.distanceEffect: Short-range cargo passage.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Synchronize separated mouths with stable orientation and chronology constraints.
stages.physicalAdvance: Paired stations, precision clocks and mouth-state telemetry.
stages.distanceEffect: Reliable long-range fixed infrastructure transit.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Model high-throughput throat dynamics under varying vessel mass and traffic.
stages.physicalAdvance: Large throat radii, thermal plants, traffic control and redundant field sectors.
stages.distanceEffect: Strategic fleet throughput replaces individual-drive range.
stages.safetyEffect: Traffic scheduling and aperture exclusion become core safety systems.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Optimize network flow, synchronization and alternate routing across many gates.
stages.physicalAdvance: Standardized mouths, network clocks and distributed scheduling.
stages.distanceEffect: Network topology, not ship speed, drives strategic mobility.
stages.maintenanceEffect: Fleetwide standards and network health monitoring.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Maintain stable throat solutions across extreme baseline/reference conditions.
stages.physicalAdvance: Higher-authority field materials, deep-space anchors and massive reserve power.
stages.distanceEffect: Very long fixed strategic links.
stages.safetyEffect: Deep redundancy and conservative chronology margins.
stages.signatureEffect: Very high but localized infrastructure signature.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Continuously solve throat geometry, traffic and recovery as one adaptive control problem.
stages.physicalAdvance: Distributed smart aperture media and autonomous local stabilization.
stages.distanceEffect: Higher uptime and throughput at smaller per-link support burden.
stages.safetyEffect: Local faults are isolated before network cascade.
stages.maintenanceEffect: Predictive replacement and reference auditing replace constant manual tuning.
stages.signatureEffect: Cleaner aperture control but persistent gate topology remains obvious.

families.operator: Map a protected macroscopic state to a compatible nonlocal target state while preserving required identity/continuity invariants.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Demonstrate controlled nonlocal mapping of simple prepared states.
stages.physicalAdvance: Fixed state-preparation and readout apparatus.
stages.distanceEffect: Microscopic state transfer only.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Extend compatibility mapping to increasingly complex bounded matter states.
stages.physicalAdvance: Larger state cages, isolation and high-capacity reference storage.
stages.distanceEffect: Macroscopic local displacement.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Preserve defined continuity invariants over complex payloads and longer separations.
stages.physicalAdvance: Whole-payload phase enclosure and stronger recovery/reconciliation systems.
stages.distanceEffect: Reliable chamber-to-chamber transfer.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Resolve remote compatible target state against authenticated beacon observations.
stages.physicalAdvance: Shipboard state cage, beacon links and endpoint occupancy sensing.
stages.distanceEffect: First vessel-scale interstellar displacement.
stages.signatureEffect: Correlated beacon and vessel phase event.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Infer target compatibility without a fully prepared receiver.
stages.physicalAdvance: Higher-resolution sensing, onboard state models and stronger cages.
stages.distanceEffect: Greatly expanded destination flexibility.
stages.signatureEffect: Larger local sensing/preparation footprint but less infrastructure signature.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Optimize target-state compatibility over long baselines and imperfect observations.
stages.physicalAdvance: Strategic reference networks, better state buffers and recovery authority.
stages.distanceEffect: Long-baseline strategic displacement with bounded uncertainty.
stages.safetyEffect: Multiple independent state proofs and fallback targets.
stages.maintenanceEffect: Data provenance, buffer health and identity safeguards dominate.

stages.mathematicalAdvance: Continuously solve identity/continuity constraints and target compatibility in compact real time.
stages.physicalAdvance: Dense state-active materials and redundant local reference stores.
stages.distanceEffect: Small platforms gain high-quality autonomous displacement.
stages.maintenanceEffect: Reference trust and state-media health dominate.

canonSafeguards: Do not infer a race, polity, manufacturer or named vessel's FTL family from technology basis alone.
Do not convert Path stage labels into arbitrary speed multipliers; each gain must name the changed mathematical or physical limit.
Do not promote DERIVED patent histories, educational lineages or machinery details to CONFIRMED without a surviving higher-authority source.
Preserve family-specific gravity sensitivity, safety horizon and failure anatomy; do not normalize them into one generic FTL difficulty model.
Numeric coefficients remain PROPOSED unless separately adopted by authoritative setting material or runtime definitions.
The inertial-torch baseline is not included among the eight true FTL development lineages and must remain conventional/relativistic comparison technology.
